items.title: "Papa Jack" Laine, Mrs. "Papa Jack" Laine and Johnny Wiggs Interview, 1959-02-27
items.q: I went with Fisher, and I had his band up all around.

ctx.x: . The time they play in all that jazz stuff, there's too much breaks in it. Let me see. You know what I mean, Johnny? Yeah. It's not the right time at all at all. Yeah. I'm going to move your chair up. Yeah, that's... That sounded like... Beautiful, beautiful. That sounded like the old-time bands, didn't it? Don't miss it. Don't miss it. It was a lot of fun to play in those days. How come the drum beat came back to you so quickly? It's just... It was just natural that the drum beat came back to you, huh? No,…
What do you want to get out? What do you want to get?

items.title: "Papa Jack" Laine Interview, 1957-03-26
items.q: I had a fellow by the name of Fisher who was playing clarinet.

ctx.x: Did you play much, uh, jobs as advertising? Do much advertising? Plenty.

Fights and balls and stuff like that. Oh yeah, plenty. Plenty advertising wagons for fights and balls and stuff like that. You know. Advertising wagons for football players too. You know, for game football players and all that sort of stuff. Yeah, played lots of advertising wagons. Plenty of them. I'll never forget the day that I played for the, um, John Ruskin Segoe advertisement on Canal Street. I had a fellow by the name of Fisher who was playing clarinet. He, it was some kind of a, a nail or something on the…

items.title: "Papa Jack" Laine and Mrs. "Papa Jack" Laine Interview, 1960-05-23
items.q: Johnny Fisher played there not much.

ctx.x: You know any other band that played over the river? Fisher played over there, didn't he?
Johnny Fisher played there not much. No. I don't know. I thought he would. No, I don't. Outside of Johnny Fisher. No. I don't.
Did you ever hear of a band, a colored band over there by the name of Minetta Band?
